newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Felderhof says can't comment for now on Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Felderhof says can't comment for now on Bre-X.

text.p: A day after Bre-X Minerals Ltd. filed for bankruptcy, its ousted chief of exploration said he could not comment now on the Busang gold scandal but may talk soon.
"I am under legal counsel not to make any statement to the press," John Felderhof said on Friday in an interview in the Cayman Islands.
He added, "I will probably be able to make a statement in the near future."
It was Felderhof's first public comments since he issued a faxed statement on Sunday denying any responsibility in the Busang scandal.
Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X said late on Thursday that Felderhof resigned from the company and the board of directors at its request.

Felderhof, 56, was named Canada's Prospector of the Year in March for his work in finding the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia, once touted as the century's biggest gold discovery. But in a devastating report on Sunday, a consultant hired by Bre-X concluded that Busang was falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining."
Felderhof said in the interview that he had no comment on anything regarding Bre-X. He also declined comment on his removal from the company.

In a statement late on Sunday faxed from a Grand Cayman hotel, Felderhof said he was "shocked and dismayed" by the consultant's report, which concluded there was massive tampering at the site, deep in the Borneo jungle.
"I know that I was not involved in a fraud. I also find it very hard to believe that anyone on my staff was involved in a fraud," Felderhof said.
The Royal Canadian Mounted Police have launched a probe into the Bre-X affair, called the biggest mining scandal in history, after receiving two fraud complaints earlier this week.
Meanwhile, Felderhof is at his $2.9 million estate in an exclusive section of Grand Cayman island. Cayman immigration officials said earlier this week Felderhof had applied for permanent residency.
The Caymans, a British territory in the western Caribbean, are known as a worldwide offshore financial centre, tax haven and tourist destination.
Felderhof and his wife, Ingrid, arrived on the island from Canada on April 22, according to immigration records, about a week before the Bre-X storm ripped through the mining world.
The Felderhofs also own a $1.25 million beachfront condominium in the island's exclusive Seven Mile Beach tourist area, as well as a house worth $433,000 in the upscale Snug Harbour section.
According to the documents, Felderhof transferred ownership in all the properties to his wife on June 6, 1996.
